# 01c: Tool use with a schema generated by @function_tool

Concept: 01a and 01b both hand-wrote a tool's JSON schema — first as a raw
dict, then generated from a Pydantic model. This variant generates the same
schema a third way: decorate a plain function with the **OpenAI Agents
SDK**'s `@function_tool` and it reads the name, description, and JSON
schema straight off the function's own type hints and docstring. No
`CountLetterArgs` class, no `model_json_schema()` call, no hand-typed dict.

The call/response round trip itself is still hand-written here, the same
`client.responses.create(...)` / `function_call_output` pattern as 01a and
01b. `@function_tool` only replaces how the schema is produced; it does not
require an `Agent` or a `Runner`. Those two pieces automate the dispatch
loop itself (call the tool, feed the result back, repeat until the model is
done) — genuinely useful once a question needs several tool calls in a row,
which is exactly the subject of the next lesson, the agent loop. Reaching
for `Agent`/`Runner` here, for a single tool call, would hide the very
round trip this lesson is trying to show.

## The three ways to get a schema, and what changed over the course

01a, 01b, and 01c are the same escalation you will see again later in the
course: the same idea gets easier to produce as the tools around it
mature. 01a hand-types the schema because that is what the wire format
looks like with nothing hidden. 01b reads the schema off a Pydantic model
instead of typing it twice. 01c reads it straight off the function
signature and docstring, no intermediate class at all. Lesson 2 goes a
step further still: once `Agent` and `Runner` are introduced there, the
entire round trip in this file — call the API, notice the function call,
run the real function, send the result back — is handled for you.

## Compare with

- `01a_function_calling_json.py` — hand-typed schema, manual dispatch.
- `01b_function_calling_pydantic.py` — Pydantic-generated schema, manual
  dispatch, same plain `client.responses.create` calls as 01a.

## Endpoint

OpenAI Responses API (`client.responses.create`), the same as 01a and 01b.
`agents.function_tool` is used only to generate the tool's schema.

## Troubleshooting

If you see `TypeError: process() takes no keyword arguments` from `httpx2`
when running this demo, your environment has the plain `Brotli` package
installed instead of `brotlicffi`. Fix with:

```
pip uninstall -y Brotli
pip install brotlicffi
```

## Regeneration prompt

If the Agents SDK changes, ask an LLM assistant: "Update this script to
match the current OpenAI Agents SDK. Keep `@function_tool` used only to
generate the `count_letter` schema, the manual `client.responses.create`
round trip (no `Agent`, no `Runner`), and the letter-counting question."
